startup.name: Multiplier
startup.description: Multiplier is an AI platform for institutional investors, starting with independent equity funds managing 250M to 5B dollars. It unifies structured and unstructured data, AI work, human work and firm knowledge in one governed application. The description claims six live hedge fund customers who spend four or more hours a day in it. Customers pay software and deployment fees. Three founders in New York.

yc_acceptance.basis: In this test the company is assumed accepted to YC for Spring 2026. Prior is about 1 percent. Live usage at six paying looking funds is real traction, and the buyer is clear, which is a strong upward factor, but a three person team in a crowded AI finance space limits it. About 4 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because six small hedge fund customers is a thin market, sales cycles to funds are long, and well funded competitors such as Rogo and Hebbia already serve finance. Partners may doubt that three founders can handle forward deployed custom work.

anchors.adjustment_reason: 1.2x the 59 percent B2B anchor: live customers with heavy daily usage is traction that the typical YC company does not have at batch start, and AI finance has seen strong seed demand.

ladder.why_it_fails: A seed fails if investors see a services heavy deployment business with six customers rather than software, or if hedge fund buyers will not give references. Trata and Constant in the YC data, both AI desks for funds, show one reaching a seed and the other no recorded round, so even good traction is not enough.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A requires moving beyond six small funds to a repeatable sales motion, and hedge funds have long compliance reviews, high customization demands and few buyers per segment. Constant and Fintool show how AI buy side tools often end as small businesses or acquisitions, and Rogo and Hebbia have raised far more.

ladder.why_it_fails: Few buy side software companies reach a Series C because the customer count is limited and incumbents with data advantages bundle AI tools. Acquisition by a data vendor is the more common end for companies at this stage.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The company fails to reach a meaningful exit if hedge funds build or buy general agents instead, if the target segment of mid size funds is too small to support venture scale revenue, or if a funded competitor like Rogo or Hebbia moves down market.

killers.evidence: Custom firm knowledge integration means each fund needs work, which hurts margins and growth.
killers.mitigation: Productize onboarding and price on usage.

killers.risk: Well funded competitors serve the same buyers
killers.evidence: Rogo and Hebbia have raised large rounds and sell to financial institutions.
killers.mitigation: Win a niche of independent equity funds.

killers.risk: Small customer base of independent funds
killers.evidence: Funds of 250M to 5B are a limited number and long sales cycles slow growth.
killers.mitigation: Expand upmarket after the first wedge.

competition_now.traction: Reported ARR above 50M and total funding in the hundreds of millions, secondary sources

technical_complexity.rationale: A unified governed platform with agents over many data sources is substantial engineering and security work, but doable for a small team using model APIs. The hard part is data licensing and fund security reviews.

takeover_risk.rationale: Funded competitors can add similar agent features within a year and have established finance distribution.

evidence.claim: Finance AI research platforms have raised substantial funding and revenue, showing demand.
Funds buy many overlapping tools, and incumbents are consolidating.

pros.evidence: The description claims four or more hours a day per user, a rare early signal.

pros.point: Clear niche and buyer with budget
pros.evidence: Independent equity funds know AI is essential and have money for tools.

brand.name: Multiplier
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Multiplier" --era 2022+ : 10 characters, 3 syllables, real word
brand.weaknesses: Generic and common, hard to own online
brand.rationale: The name conveys leverage for analysts and is easy to say, but it is generic and widely used. For institutional buyers, trust and references matter more than the name.

narrative.headline: Real early traction in a valuable niche, but a small buyer pool and well funded rivals limit later rounds.
narrative.general_summary: Multiplier has an unusually strong early signal, six hedge funds live with long daily use, in a market where AI finance platforms have raised large sums. That makes a seed above the YC check more likely than the cohort average. The risks are a services heavy deployment, a narrow segment of mid size funds, and rivals such as Rogo and Hebbia with far more money. Later steps follow the cohort anchors with a modest uplift, and the upside path is a move upmarket to larger asset managers or a pivot to a horizontal governed agent platform. Reaching a round years later is common for B2B companies with paying customers.

assumptions: Test is blind: only the YC input file was used for company facts.
Seed means a round above $500K within about 12 months.
Customer claims in the description are unverified.
